name: Two-track UI audit: deterministic metrics, then a capped rubric verdict
description: Separate deterministic UI MEASUREMENT from design JUDGEMENT, and make the judgement answerable to the measurement. Track A fans out independent collectors - contrast, tap targets, focus-visible, dead controls, motion, Lighthouse - and each is allowed to be UNAVAILABLE, in which case its dimension scores UNKNOWN with the exclusion stated rather than silently averaged away. Track B then makes exactly ONE scoring call per rubric dimension, so no single call can trade one dimension off against another. A measured critical error CAPS the composite instead of being averaged into it, and a cross-vendor critic is reconciled by taking the MORE CONSERVATIVE of the two verdicts.

app_target.description: The LOCAL running app to audit. This workflow never edits app source.

rubric_version.description: Pinned rubric. An unpinned rubric makes two audits incomparable.

rubric_dimensions.description: One scoring CALL per entry. The one-call-per-dimension protocol is the stabiliser.

optional_engines.description: Opt-in extras (second a11y engine, real NVDA, Storybook a11y, UIClip prior). An unavailable engine excludes its dimension explicitly.

enable_codex_critic.description: Run the cross-vendor critic and reconcile conservatively.

collector.description: Track A: runs one deterministic collector and reports numbers only - never a score.

scorer.description: Track B: scores exactly ONE rubric dimension per call, reading Track A's numbers.

override-auditor.description: Applies the critical-error override: a measured critical failure CAPS the composite.

codex-critic.description: The fifth persona: an independent cross-vendor critic scoring the same dimensions from the same numbers.

routes.reason: a deterministic collector reports numbers; effort buys nothing there
the fifth persona is only worth having if it fails differently

stages.title: S0 - fan out the deterministic collectors; numbers only, no scores

work_unit.title: Run one deterministic UI collector and emit measurements without judgement
work_unit.question_or_target: Measure one property across every surface and emit raw numbers with their measurement parameters - and when the engine is unavailable, emit UNAVAILABLE with the reason instead of an empty pass.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: the measurement is mechanical, but deciding a collector is genuinely unavailable rather than merely slow is judgement

work_unit.evidence_requirement: per-surface numeric values with the measurement parameters (viewport, theme, engine and version), so a re-run is comparable
tests_required: an unavailable engine emits UNAVAILABLE with a reason and NOT an empty measurement set
no collector output contains a score - a collector that scores has crossed into Track B
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the override-auditor, which needs the raw numbers to compute the cap
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:UX-7801 emitted only when every surface has a value or an explicit UNAVAILABLE with a reason; otherwise FAILED:UX-7801 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: fixed, two attempts: a browser engine can fail to attach transiently
work_unit.mechanism: single-property deterministic measurement with explicit UNAVAILABLE accounting

stages.title: Collect what landed; a missing collector becomes a stated exclusion
An excluded dimension must SAY it was excluded
S1 - exactly ONE scoring call per rubric dimension

body.title: Score exactly one dimension, reading Track A's numbers

work_unit.title: Score one rubric dimension 0-4 against the measured numbers
work_unit.question_or_target: Score ONE dimension on the pinned rubric, citing the Track A measurement that justifies the score, and never referencing another dimension - so the call cannot trade dimensions off against each other.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: scoring is the judgement half of the two-track split and needs full reasoning effort

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the 0-4 score, the rubric anchor text for that band, and the specific Track A measurement cited
tests_required: a score that contradicts a measured failure on the same dimension is REJECTED, not averaged
each call scores exactly one dimension; a call emitting two scores fails the one-call-per-dimension gate
a dimension whose collector was UNAVAILABLE scores UNKNOWN, never a default mid-band
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the codex-critic, scoring the same dimension independently from the same numbers
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:UX-7802 emitted only when one dimension carries one score with a cited measurement, or UNKNOWN with the exclusion; otherwise FAILED:UX-7802 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: fixed, two attempts: a scoring call is cheap and a transient truncation is recoverable
work_unit.mechanism: one-call-per-dimension scoring bound to a cited measurement

stages.title: One call, one dimension - or the stabiliser is not in force
Track B may not contradict Track A's measurements
S2 - a measured critical error CAPS the composite, it is not averaged

work_unit.title: Compute the weighted composite and apply the critical-error cap
work_unit.question_or_target: Compute the weighted composite with colour-contrast weighted highest, then CAP it at the ceiling implied by any measured critical error, so a single hard failure cannot be diluted by eight good dimensions.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: the cap is the veto and belongs to the role that holds it

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the per-dimension weights, the raw weighted mean, every critical error with its measurement, and the capped result - all four so the cap is auditable arithmetic and not an assertion
tests_required: a page with a measured contrast failure has its composite CAPPED, not averaged - the raw mean and the capped value are both recorded and differ
with zero critical errors the cap is inactive and the composite equals the weighted mean, proving the cap is not a constant discount
UNKNOWN dimensions are excluded from the denominator and named, so an unavailable engine cannot inflate or deflate the mean
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the codex-critic, recomputing the composite from the same inputs
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:UX-7803 emitted only when raw mean, cap, capped composite and the critical-error list are all present; otherwise FAILED:UX-7803 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: none: the composite is arithmetic over recorded inputs, so a retry cannot change it
work_unit.mechanism: weighted composite with a hard critical-error ceiling and UNKNOWN exclusion from the denominator

stages.title: The composite must actually respect the cap
S3 - reconcile with the cross-vendor critic, taking the MORE CONSERVATIVE verdict

impact.blast_radius: READ-ONLY by construction: Edit and every app-source write path are denied, so the audit cannot change what it measures

bp7.why_not_deterministic: Track A is deterministic and cached; Track B is model judgement stabilised by the one-call-per-dimension protocol rather than by a seed, so the workflow declares deterministic:false and verifies semantically.

worked_example.scenario: Audit momentstudio's settings page. One label measures 3.1:1 contrast - a WCAG AA failure - while the other eight dimensions are strong.
expected_trace: collect-track-a -> 8 of 9 collectors land; lighthouse-cwv times out at the deadline barrier and proceeds degraded
track-a-join -> quorum 0.89 >= 0.6 PASS; exclusion-gate -> the 'motion' dimension is marked UNKNOWN with 'lighthouse-cwv UNAVAILABLE: deadline' stated
score-track-b -> 8 dimensions scored in 8 separate calls (3 concurrent); motion scores UNKNOWN
protocol-gate PASS (8 calls, 8 dimensions, 0 multi-dimension calls)
consistency-gate PASS - no score contradicts a measurement
apply-critical-override -> raw weighted mean 3.4/4; the 3.1:1 contrast measurement is a critical error with a cap of 2.0; capped composite = 2.0. BOTH numbers are recorded
reconcile-with-critic -> Codex scores hierarchy 2 where Claude scored 3; the conservative rule takes 2
worked_example.expected_terminal_state: SUCCESS:UX-7803 with composite 2.0 (capped from 3.4) and 1 dimension UNKNOWN

bp7.unverified: UNVERIFIED whether the cross-vendor reconciliation changes outcomes often enough to pay for itself; settling experiment = compare solo and reconciled verdicts on ten screens and count how many times the conservative rule changed the verdict band, not merely a score.
bp7.council_expression_encoding_note: The council stopping rule must parse under BOTH the DSL grammar and councilspec's metric registry (DSL-SEM-014). Measured 2026-08-10: the DSL tokenizer rejects ':' at offset 6, so councilspec's `custom:<name>` escape hatch is NOT usable inside a DSL council stage, and the rule text is restricted to the 51 registry metrics. `minority_report_present == true` is therefore the registry encoding of 'both verdicts were recorded' - the less-conservative verdict is preserved as the minority report rather than being overwritten by the conservative one. `all_participants_spoke == true` encodes 'the critic actually scored'. This is an encoding constraint, not a weaker guarantee, but the mapping is stated here so a reader does not take the metric name literally.

distinct_from.BP-CNC-06: that is the GENERAL rubric engine distilled from this; this is the UI-specific instrument with its own deterministic Track A
distinct_from.bp-ux-01: that is the pipeline that calls this as G3; this never edits source and has no revert gate because it has nothing to revert
distinct_from.bp-ux-03: that audits SOURCE and cannot see a computed contrast value; this measures the running app
